methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved dissecting the text into discrete statements about the circuit's functionality, inputs, outputs, and timing behavior. Overlapping or redundant statements were merged or refined to ensure each atomic unit represented a unique aspect of the design.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Create a 16-bit register using D flip-flops.
When byteena[1] is asserted (1), the upper byte is updated with d[15:8] at the rising edge of the clock.
When byteena[0] is asserted (1), the lower byte is updated with d[7:0] at the rising edge of the clock.
When a byte-enable input is deasserted (0), the corresponding byte retains its previous value.
The register has a synchronous, active-low reset input 'resetn'.
When 'resetn' is low at the rising edge of the clock, all 16 flip-flops are reset to 0.
All D flip-flops are triggered by the positive edge of clk.
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has inputs clk, resetn, byteena[1:0], d[15:0] and output q[15:0].
q is a 16-bit register.
byteena controls selective updates to q.
d is the 16-bit data input.
resetn is an active-low synchronous reset.
clk is the clock input.
Combinational logic determines the next state of each bit in q.
When resetn is low (0), all bits of q are set to 0 synchronously.
byteena[0] controls the lower byte (bits 7:0).
byteena[1] controls the upper byte (bits 15:8).
If resetn == 0: q[i]_next = 0 (reset condition).
If resetn == 1 and (i < 8 && byteena[0] == 1): q[i]_next = d[i] (lower byte update).
If resetn == 1 and (i >= 8 && byteena[1] == 1): q[i]_next = d[i] (upper byte update).
Otherwise: q[i]_next = q[i] (no update, retain current value).
q changes only on the positive edge of clk.
When resetn is low on a rising clk edge, q is set to 0.
When resetn is high on a rising clk edge, the value of q is updated based on byteena.
If byteena[0] is high, q[7:0] is updated with d[7:0].
If byteena[1] is high, q[15:8] is updated with d[15:8].
If a byte enable is low, the corresponding byte of q retains its previous value.
There is a setup time requirement for resetn, byteena, and d with respect to the rising edge of clk.
The reset signal resetn must be stable before the rising edge of clk.
The data input d and byte enable inputs byteena must also be stable before the rising edge of clk.
The circuit contains 16 D flip-flops.
The flip-flops are positive-edge triggered.
The reset is synchronous.
The byte enables control which bytes of the register are updated on each clock cycle.
